clue.text: Choose not to use key cut with sharp instrument

parts.note: ESC is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to cut with an axe or similar blade

explanation.surface: Someone declines a key that has been cut with a sharp tool, as a locksmith might.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to avoid or abstain from it deliberately, a synonym.

clue.text: Competition plan loses backing a bit late in the day

definitions.text: a bit late in the day

parts.note: an event is a contest

indicators.note: loses backing means the word drops its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: A tournament's scheme drops its sponsors rather late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing looks like financial support, but it is the back letter of the word for plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, a slightly late part of the day.

clue.text: Provide food box after taking down recipe

indicators.note: taking down means that letter is moved lower, to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a crate is a box
R is short for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A caterer supplies a food hamper after noting down a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply meals for an event, so it means to serve or furnish eats.

clue.text: Name one story about consuming love and joy

indicators.note: consuming means the other letter is swallowed inside
about means the whole is turned round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tale is a story
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone names a romance story, all about love and joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns N, I and TALE round to give ELATIN, and 'consuming' puts O, love as tennis's zero, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness, a close synonym.

clue.text: Everyone in the main is disorganised

parts.note: everyone is all
at, as in 'at home', means in
the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: Everybody out on the ocean is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'all at sea' literally, which is also the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: All at sea is an idiom for confused or bewildered, so it means disorganised.

clue.text: City guides in audiobook format?

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: leads means guides

explanation.surface: City tour guides now come as audiobooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Think about place to deliver speech

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a problem is to deal with it
second meaning: where post is delivered

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as pondering a venue for a talk; the three phrases are three meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers tackling an issue, a postal location and a formal oration.

clue.text: Wear false boobs being conscious of one's appearance

indicators.note: boobs means blunders, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone wears fake breasts and is very aware of how they look.
explanation.walkthrough: Boobs looks like a noun, but it is a verb: makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-aware means conscious of oneself, here of how one comes across to others.

clue.text: Items of business information original person almost absorbs

indicators.note: absorbs means the other word goes inside
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: The first person takes in information on business matters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of matters to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Combination of porridge and egg that will go off

indicators.note: combination of says the two words are joined together

parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, which is time
egg is old military slang for a bomb

explanation.surface: A breakfast of porridge and an egg that has gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time served in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A time bomb is an explosive set to detonate at a set moment, something due to explode.

clue.text: Hand over suspect information technology infiltrating former clientele

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: infiltrating means one piece gets inside the other

parts.note: a shop's trade is its customers

explanation.surface: A suspect's details from IT have crept into an old customer list.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to surrender an accused person to another country's jurisdiction.

clue.text: Dig starts to discover extraordinary lead vases everywhere

indicators.note: starts to these words means take the first letter of each of them

explanation.surface: An archaeological dig turns up remarkable lead vases all over the site.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig into the ground, or to search deeply.

clue.text: Stop abandoning North American member of colony

indicators.note: abandoning means the word for stop loses these letters

parts.note: to terminate is to stop

explanation.surface: A North American colonist gives up and quits the settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are social insects living in large colonies, so one is an example of a colony member.

clue.text: Union official set out The Guardian's responsibility

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: a ward is a person placed in a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A trade-union officer has laid out what the Guardian newspaper is responsible for.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian looks like the newspaper, but it is any guardian, whose charge is a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop steward is the trade-union representative elected by workers in a workplace.

clue.text: Get rid of people identified after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution, the word is turned round end to end

parts.note: named means identified

explanation.surface: Political opponents are purged once they have been identified after a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To deman is to reduce the staff or workforce of something, cutting personnel.

clue.text: Throne in Spanish car similar to upmarket German one?

parts.note: Merc is short for Mercedes, so Merc-y means like a Mercedes
SEAT is a Spanish car maker

explanation.surface: A seat in a Spanish car that feels like a luxury German one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is reached by a whimsical adjective: Mercy, Mercedes-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The mercy seat was the gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant, regarded as God's throne.

clue.text: Extra support to remain in place too long

parts.note: over means extra or surplus, as in 'left over'
a stay is a prop or brace

explanation.surface: An extra prop keeps something standing longer than it should.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstay is to stay beyond the welcome or the permitted time.

clue.text: Existence sucks on the whole

indicators.note: sucks means takes the other piece in

parts.note: entity means existence or being
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict that life is awful, all told.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety means the whole of something, a synonym.

clue.text: Narrow stream is not flowing in ditch

parts.note: a jet is a thin stream of liquid

indicators.note: flowing means the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A thin trickle of water is stagnant in a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: Ditch is a verb, not the trench the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard or throw away, as you ditch something.

clue.text: Block off building with club and bit of stick

parts.note: a brick is a block taken from a building
a bat is a club

explanation.surface: Someone takes a block from a building, a club and a piece of stick as weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick here is British slang for criticism, as in 'give someone stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is a critical remark, and stick is informal British for criticism.

clue.text: Fish dish using perch regularly cooked with chives mainly

indicators.note: cooked means these letters are mixed up
regularly means take every other letter of perch
mainly means drop the last letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for a perch dish cooked with chives.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceviche is a Latin American dish of raw fish cured in citrus juice.

clue.text: Former magistrate's expression of doubt over first-time offender

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: er is a hesitant noise of doubt
Eve committed the first sin in the Bible story

explanation.surface: An old magistrate hesitates over sentencing a first offender.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in Anglo-Saxon England, a chief magistrate of a town or district.

clue.text: Perhaps get fed up again with English person choosing not to work

parts.note: re-tire, to tire again, cryptically gives this word, hence Perhaps

explanation.surface: An English worker gets bored again and stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: The question of the definition: retire normally means stop work; read as RE-TIRE it means grow weary once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree has left employment, someone who no longer works.

clue.text: Making a killing in America in the near future?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in US slang to off someone is to kill them
second meaning: the ..., as in 'in the ...', is the near future

explanation.walkthrough: Making a killing looks like making money; the question mark flags that the second sense needs the phrase 'in the offing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is American slang for murdering, and also the part of the sea visible near the horizon, hence soon to come.

clue.text: Remaining on smart section of motorway?

indicators.note: on means the first word is placed after the second, as in a down clue

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or smart
over means remaining, as in 'left over'

explanation.surface: Something left behind on a stylish stretch of road.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyover is a bridge carrying one road over another, a part of a motorway system; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Breed fish one's caught

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rays are flat fish, and fish can be plural

explanation.surface: An angler breeds the fish they have landed.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught looks like the angler's catch, but it means caught by the ear, heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise animals is to rear or breed them.

clue.text: Head of state returned to deal with military action

indicators.note: returned means the letters are turned back

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the British head of state
to treat is to deal with

explanation.surface: A returning head of state handles a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is the withdrawal of troops, an action in warfare.

clue.text: 24 is convoluted tale about unknown quantity

definitions.note: the answer to 24, a verb meaning lift up

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the shuffled story goes round the unknown
convoluted means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: x is the standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A twisted story about an unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to elevate or lift high, so it means to raise in rank or praise.

clue.text: Part of high-profile actor associated with part of …

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a famous actor is linked with a section of the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into 28: the definition reads 'associated with part of … entrails', the ileum being part of the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac is the adjective relating to the ileum, a portion of the small intestine.

clue.text: … name associated with entrails possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 27, a name gets linked to guts.
explanation.walkthrough: N plus ENTRAILS rearranged gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: entrails are what internals possibly means.
explanation.definitionFit: Internals are the inner organs, so entrails or guts are one example.

clue.text: Learned that woman did not let out skirts

indicators.note: skirts means the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: gated means confined, as a student kept in college
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A seamstress has learned that a woman refused to let out her skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirts is a verb here, not clothing, though 'gathered skirts' and 'let out' feed the sewing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered means understood or inferred, as in 'I gathered he was leaving', the same as learned.

clue.text: Rude message about church employee

parts.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone working for the church gets an indecent text.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is the official who looks after a church and its graveyard.
